stem: A ring which can slide along the rod is kept at the mid point of a smooth rod of length L. The rod is rotated with constant angular velocity ω about a vertical axis passing through one of its ends. The ring is released from the mid point. Find (a) the acceleration of the ring w.r.t. the rod when it is at a distance x from the axis, (b) the velocity of the ring when it just leaves the rod.

The minimum speed v with which a small ball should be pushed inside a smooth vertical tube of radius R from a height h such that it may reach the top of the tube is: (a) √(2g(h+2R)) (b) (5/2)R (c) √(g(5R−2h)) (d) √(2g(2R−h))

A smooth sphere of radius R is made to translate in a straight line with a constant acceleration a. A particle kept on the top of the sphere is released from there at zero velocity with respect to the sphere. Find the speed of the particle with respect to the sphere as a function of the angle θ it slides. (a) [2R(a sinθ + g − g cosθ)] 1/2 (b) [2R(a cosθ + g − g sinθ)] 1/2 (c) [2R(g sinθ + a − g cosθ)] 1/2 (d) [2R(g cosθ + a − g sinθ)] 1/2

Passage (Q4–Q6): A small block of mass m is projected horizontally from the top of a smooth fixed hemisphere of radius r with speed u. For u ≥ u 0 (u 0 = √(gr)) it does not slide on the hemisphere, i.e. it leaves the surface at the top itself. — For u = 2u 0 it lands at point P on the ground. Find OP. (a) √2 r (b) 2r (c) 4r (d) 2√2 r
For u = u 0 /3, find the height from the ground at which it leaves the hemisphere. (a) 19r/9 (b) 19r/27 (c) 10r/9 (d) 10r/27

key: c g — at N = 0 gravity is the only force acting
stem: Find its net acceleration at the instant it leaves the hemisphere. (a) −g (b) g/2 (c) g (d) g/3

Passage (Q7 & Q8): A small block of mass M starts sliding down on a bigger block of mass 2M having a circular track of radius R. Let N 1 and N 2 be the normal reactions on the bigger block due to the wall and the floor. Do not consider the motion of the small block after θ = 90°; all surfaces are frictionless. — The value of N 1 at the instant when θ = 30°. (a) √3Mg/4 (b) 3√3Mg/4 (c) √3Mg/2 (d) 3√3Mg/2
The value of tanθ at the instant when N 2 = 3Mg. (a) 1/√2 (b) √2 (c) 1 (d) 2

A small block of mass m rests on top of a hemispherical wedge of radius R. The wedge is given a constant acceleration a 0 = g in the horizontal direction as shown in the figure. If the velocity of the block relative to the wedge at the instant it breaks contact with the surface is √(2gR/n), then find the value of n.

A particle P is moving on a circle under the action of only one force, which always acts towards a fixed point O lying on the circumference. Find the ratio of d²θ/dt² to (dθ/dt)² at the moment when θ = 45°. (C is the centre of the circle.)

A table with smooth horizontal surface is placed in a cabin which moves in a circle of large radius R (angular velocity ω). A smooth pulley of small radius is fastened to the table. Two masses m 1 = m and m 2 = 2m are placed on the table connected through a string going over the pulley. Initially the masses were at rest. Find the magnitude of the initial acceleration of the masses as seen from the cabin and the tension in the string.

A particle of mass m is fixed to one end of a light spring of force constant k and unstretched length ℓ. The system is rotated about the other end of the spring with an angular velocity ω in gravity-free space. The increase in length of the spring will be: (a) mω²ℓ/k (b) mω²ℓ/(k − mω²) (c) mω²ℓ/(k + mω²) (d) None of these

A smooth wire is bent into a vertical circle of radius a. A bead P can slide smoothly on the wire. The circle is rotated about diameter AB as axis with a speed ω as shown in the figure. The bead P is at rest with respect to the circular ring in the position shown (P at a distance a/2 from the axis). Then ω is equal to: (a) (2g/a) 1/2 (b) [2g/(√3a)] 1/2 (c) (√3g/a) 1/2 (d) (g/2a) 1/2

A circular turn table of radius 0.5 m has a smooth groove as shown in the figure. A ball of mass 90 g is placed inside the groove along with a spring of spring constant 10² N/cm. The ball is at a distance of 0.1 m from the centre when the turn table is at rest. On rotating the turn table with a constant angular velocity of 10² rad/sec, the ball moves away from the initial position by a distance nearly equal to: (a) 10 −1 m (b) 10 −2 m (c) 10 −3 m (d) 2×10 −1 m

A skier plans to ski a smooth fixed hemisphere of radius R. He starts from rest from a curved smooth surface of height R/4. The angle θ at which he leaves the hemisphere is: (a) cos −1 (2/3) (b) cos −1 (5/√3) (c) cos −1 (5/6) (d) cos −1 (5/2√3)

Figure shows a smooth track in a vertical plane, consisting of two circular arcs AB and BC of the same radius = 2 m. The common tangent to the arcs, BD, is horizontal. A small block placed on the track at a height h above BD leaves the track at exactly the same depth below. Determine h (in cm).

key: 4 m (r max = 4.5 m, r min = 0.5 m)
stem: Two equal masses m each are attached by a string. One mass lies at radial distance r from the centre of a horizontal turn-table which rotates with constant angular velocity ω = 2 rad s −1 , while the other mass hangs from the string inside the turn-table's hollow spindle. The coefficient of static friction between the turn-table and the mass lying on it is μ s = 0.8. The maximum and minimum values of r such that the mass lying on the turn-table does not slide are r max and r min . Find the value of (r max − r min ) in metre.

A point mass m connected to one end of an inextensible string of length ℓ, the other end of the string being fixed at a peg. The string is free to rotate in a vertical plane. Find the minimum velocity given to the mass in the horizontal direction so that it hits the peg in its subsequent motion. (a) [(3+√2)gℓ] 1/2 (b) [(2+√3)gℓ] 1/2 (c) [(1+2√3)gℓ] 1/2 (d) [(1+2√2)gℓ] 1/2

A person rolls a small ball with speed u along the floor from point A. If x = 3R, determine the required speed u so that the ball returns to A after rolling on the circular surface in the vertical plane from B to C and becoming a projectile at C. (a) 2√(gR) (b) √(5gR) (c) √(6gR) (d) (5/2)√(gR)

key: a The ratio is a constant 2/3 — the horizontal-line graph, option (a)
stem: A small particle of mass m is released from rest from point A inside a smooth hemispherical bowl as shown. The ratio (x) of the magnitude of the centripetal force and the normal reaction on the particle at any point B varies as: (four graphs of x against θ are offered)

A solid body rotates about a stationary axis so that its angular velocity depends on the rotation angle φ as ω = ω 0 − kφ, where ω 0 and k are positive constants. At the moment t = 0 the angle φ = 0. Find the time dependence of the rotation angle. (a) kω 0 e −kt (b) (ω 0 /k)e −kt (c) (ω 0 /k)(1 − e −kt ) (d) (k/ω 0 )(e −kt − 1)

A small block is connected to one end of two identical massless strings of length 16⅔ cm each with their other ends fixed to a vertical rod. If the ratio of tensions T 1 /T 2 is 4:1, then what will be the angular speed ω of the block? (the lower string makes 60° with the rod) (a) 10 rad/s (b) 14 rad/s (c) 15 rad/s (d) 20 rad/s

A particle is hanging from a fixed point O by means of a string of length a. There is a small smooth nail O′ in the same horizontal line with O at a distance b (b < a) from O. The minimum velocity with which the particle should be projected from its lowest position in order that it may make a complete revolution round the nail without the string becoming slack: (a) √(5g(a−b)) (b) √(3(a−b)g) (c) √((5a−3b)g) (d) √((7a−3b)g)

A circular platform rotates around a vertical axis with an angular velocity of 10 rad/s. On the platform is a ball of mass 1 kg, attached to the long axis of the platform by a thin rod of length 10 cm (α = 30°). Find the normal force exerted by the ball on the platform (in N). Friction is absent.

In the figure shown, a lift goes downwards with a constant retardation. An observer in the lift observes a conical pendulum in the lift, revolving in a horizontal circle with time period 2 s. The distance between the centre of the circle and the point of suspension is 2.0 m. Find the retardation of the lift in m/s². Use π² = 10 and g = 10 m/s².

In the system shown, the mass m = 2 kg oscillates in a circular arc of amplitude 60°. The minimum value of the coefficient of friction between the block of mass 8 kg and the surface of the table to avoid slipping is: (a) 0.25 (b) 0.50 (c) 0.40 (d) None of these

A heavy particle hangs from a point O by a string of length a. It is projected horizontally with a velocity u = √((2+√3)ag). The angle with the downward vertical that the string makes when it becomes slack is: (a) θ = sin −1 (−1/√3) (b) θ = cos −1 (−1/√3) (c) θ = cos −1 (−1/√2) (d) θ = sin −1 (−1/√2)

Two point masses m are connected by a light rod of length 2ℓ and it is free to rotate in a vertical plane as shown (one mass at ℓ and one at 2ℓ from the pivot). Calculate the minimum horizontal velocity to be given to the lower mass, so that it completes the circular motion in the vertical plane. (a) √(48gℓ/5) (b) √(10gℓ) (c) √(6gℓ) (d) √(24gℓ/5)

A circular tube of mass M is placed vertically on a horizontal surface as shown. Two small spheres of mass m, just fit in the tube, are released from the top. If θ is the angle between the radius vector of either ball with the vertical, then find the ratio m/M if the tube breaks its contact with the ground when θ = 60°. Neglect friction. (a) 1/2 (b) 4 (c) 2 (d) 6

A collar of mass m is tied at one end of a spring of spring constant mg/R and unstretched length R/2, the other end being tied to a fixed point O. The smooth semicircular wire frame is fixed in a vertical plane. Find the normal reaction between the collar and the wire just before it reaches the lowest point. (a) 3mg (b) 4mg (c) 5mg (d) 6mg

A small wedge whose base is horizontal is fixed to a vertical rod as shown in the figure. The sloping side of the wedge is frictionless and the wedge is spun with an angular speed ω about the vertical axis. Find ω so that the block does not slip relative to the wedge. (a) √(g tanθ/ℓ) (b) √(g sinθ/(ℓcos²θ)) (c) √(g cosθ/(ℓsinθ)) (d) √(g cotθ/ℓ)

Two blocks A (mass 4m, at 2ℓ) and B (mass m, at ℓ) are connected by a cord passing around a frictionless pulley which is attached to a rotating frame. Determine the value of ω at which the blocks start sliding radially. (a) √(3μg/7ℓ) (b) √(5μg/9ℓ) (c) √(5μg/7ℓ) (d) √(μg/3ℓ)

A particle is attached with a string of length ℓ which is fixed at point O on an inclined plane. What minimum velocity should be given to the particle along the incline so that it may complete a circle on the inclined plane (plane is smooth and initially the particle was resting on the inclined plane, angle 30°)? (a) √(5gℓ) (b) √(5gℓ/2) (c) √(5√3gℓ/2) (d) √(4gℓ)

A particle is projected at an angle θ with the horizontal. What is the radius of curvature of the parabola traced out by the projectile at a point where the particle velocity makes an angle θ/2 with the horizontal? (a) u²cos²θ/(g cos³(θ/2)) (b) u²cos²θ/(g sin³(θ/2)) (c) u²cos²θ/(g cos²(θ/2)sin(θ/2)) (d) u²cos²θ/(g sin²(θ/2)cos(θ/2))

Multiple Correct Answer Question. A plank is moving along the X-axis with constant velocity v 0 . A pendulum having a bob of mass m and length ℓ is performing circular motion about O on the plank with speed v 0 with respect to the plank as shown in the figure. At t = 0 the particle velocity is along the Y axis, then: (a) work done by tension on the particle with respect to the plank is zero for any time interval (b) work done by tension on the particle with respect to the ground in time πℓ/2v 0 is +mv 0 ² (c) work done by tension on the particle in time 2πℓ/v 0 in the ground frame is −2πmv 0 ² (d) work done by tension on the particle in time πℓ/v 0 in the ground frame is zero

Passage (Q1 & Q2): A block of mass m moves on a horizontal circle against the wall of a cylindrical room of radius R. The floor of the room on which the block moves is smooth but the friction coefficient between the block and the side wall is μ. The block is given initial velocity v 0 . — What is the value of velocity v as a function of the distance s travelled on the circumference? (a) v = v 0 e −2μs/R (b) v = v 0 e −μs/R (c) v = v 0 (1 − e −2μs/R ) (d) v = v 0
What is the time taken by the block to complete the first revolution? (a) (R/μv 0 )(e 2μπ − 1) (b) (2R/μv 0 )(e 2μπ − 1) (c) 2Re 2μπ /(μv 0 ) (d) Re 2μπ /(μv 0 )

There is a fixed smooth hemisphere of radius R. A rod AB is placed as shown in the figure. When end A of the rod is at a distance x 1 from the centre of the hemisphere and has velocity v A in the horizontal direction, the angular speed of the rod is found as nv A R/(x 1 √(x 1 ²−R²)). Find n. (Assume all surfaces are smooth.)

Two beads of mass m and 2m are connected by a massless rod of length R and threaded onto a smooth circular wire of radius R. When the wire rotates uniformly with angular velocity ω about a vertical diameter, the beads do not slide on it and the rod remains vertical as shown. What must be the angular velocity ω (in rad/s) of the wire? (Take R = 15 m)

Multiple Correct Answer Question. Two particles each of mass m are attached to the two ends of a light string of length L, which passes through a hole at the centre of a smooth table. One particle describes a circular path on the table with angular velocity ω 1 and the other describes a conical pendulum with angular velocity ω 2 below the table. If ℓ 1 and ℓ 2 are the lengths of the portions of the string above and below the table, then: (a) ℓ 1 /ℓ 2 = ω 2 /ω 1 (b) ℓ 1 /ℓ 2 = (ω 2 /ω 1 )² (c) 1/ω 1 ² + 1/ω 2 ² = mℓ/g (d) 1/ω 1 ² + 1/ω 2 ² = ℓcosθ/g

Multiple Correct Answer Question. One end of a thread of length ℓ = 1 m is attached to an inclined plane of angle of elevation α. A point-like body of mass m = 1 kg is attached to the other end. The body is released without initial speed, such that the thread is tight and horizontal. The coefficient of friction between the slope and the body is μ. (a) The tension in the thread, when the angle between the thread and the horizontal is φ, is T = mg(3sinφsinα − 2μφcosα) (b) The tension will be maximum when φ = 90° (c) The tension will be maximum when φ = cos −1 (2μ/(3tanα)) (d) The maximum speed of the particle will be when φ = cos −1 (μcotα)

In case of vertical circular motion of a particle by a thread of length r, if the tension in the thread is zero at an angle 30° shown in the figure, the velocity at the bottom point (A) of the circular path is (g = gravitational acceleration): (a) √(5gr) (b) √(7gr/2) (c) √(4gr) (d) √(5gr/2) — (JEE Main 2026, 24 Jan Shift 2)

A large drum having radius R is spinning around its axis with angular velocity ω. The minimum value of ω so that a body of mass M remains stuck to the inner wall of the drum, taking the coefficient of friction between the drum surface and mass M as μ, is: (a) √(μg/R) (b) √(2g/μR) (c) √(g/2μR) (d) √(g/μR) — (JEE Main 2026, 21 Jan Shift 2)

key: b 2 (v B ² = 4gℓ, v C ² = 2gℓ)
stem: A bob of mass m is suspended at a point O by a light string of length ℓ and left to perform vertical circular motion as shown in the figure. Initially, by applying horizontal velocity v 0 at point A, the string becomes slack when the bob reaches point D. The ratio of the kinetic energy of the bob at the points B and C is ______. (OC is 60° from OD and OB is 60° from OC) (a) 1 (b) 2 (c) 4 (d) 3 — (JEE Main 2025)

key: c μ = (v 0 ² − rg tanθ)/(rg + v 0 ²tanθ)
stem: A car of mass m moves on a banked road having radius r and banking angle θ. To avoid slipping from the banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is v 0 . The coefficient of friction μ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is: (a) μ = (v 0 ²+rg tanθ)/(rg+v 0 ²tanθ) (b) μ = (v 0 ²−rg tanθ)/(rg−v 0 ²tanθ) (c) μ = (v 0 ²−rg tanθ)/(rg+v 0 ²tanθ) (d) μ = (v 0 ²+rg tanθ)/(rg−v 0 ²tanθ) — (JEE Main 2025)

A body of mass m connected to a massless and unstretchable string goes in a vertical circle of radius R under gravity g. The other end of the string is fixed at the centre of the circle. If the velocity at the top of the circular path is n√(gR), where n ≥ 1, then the ratio of the kinetic energy of the body at the bottom to that at the top of the circle is: (a) n²/(n²+4) (b) (n²+4)/n² (c) (n+4)/n (d) n/(n+4) — (JEE Main 2025)

A circular table is rotating with an angular velocity of ω rad/s about its axis. There is a smooth groove along a radial direction on the table. A steel ball is gently placed at a distance of 1 m on the groove. All the surfaces are smooth. If the radius of the table is 3 m, the radial velocity of the ball w.r.t. the table at the time the ball leaves the table is x√2 ω m/s, where the value of x is ______. — (JEE Main 2024)

A particle is moving in a circle of radius 50 cm in such a way that at any instant the normal and tangential components of its acceleration are equal. If its speed at t = 0 is 4 m s −1 , the time taken to complete the first revolution will be (1/α)[1 − e −2π ] s, where α = ______. — (JEE Main 2024)

A car of 800 kg is taking a turn on a banked road of radius 300 m and angle of banking 30°. If the coefficient of static friction is 0.2 then the maximum speed with which the car can negotiate the turn safely: (g = 10 m/s², √3 = 1.73) (a) 264 m/s (b) 51.4 m/s (c) 70.4 m/s (d) 102.8 m/s — (JEE Main 2024)

A bob of mass m is suspended by a light string of length L. It is imparted a minimum horizontal velocity at the lowest point A such that it just completes half a circle reaching the topmost position B. The ratio of kinetic energies (K.E.) A /(K.E.) B is: (a) 3:2 (b) 5:1 (c) 2:5 (d) 1:5 — (JEE Main 2024)

A small block of mass 100 g is tied to a spring of spring constant 7.5 N m −1 and length 20 cm. The other end of the spring is fixed at a particular point A. If the block moves in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular velocity 5 rad s −1 about point A, then the tension in the spring is: (a) 0.75 N (b) 0.25 N (c) 0.50 N (d) 1.5 N — (JEE Main 2023)

A closed circular tube of average radius 15 cm, whose inner walls are rough, is kept in a vertical plane. A block of mass 1 kg just fits inside the tube. The speed of the block is 22 m s −1 when it is introduced at the top of the tube. After completing five oscillations, the block stops at the bottom region of the tube. The work done by the tube on the block is ______ J. (g = 10 m s −2 ) — (JEE Main 2023)

A car is moving on a circular path of radius 600 m such that the magnitudes of the tangential acceleration and centripetal acceleration are equal. The time taken by the car to complete the first quarter of revolution, if it is moving with an initial speed of 54 km h −1 , is t(1 − e −π/2 ) s. The value of t is ______. — (JEE Main 2023)

A body of mass 200 g is tied to a spring of spring constant 12.5 N m −1 , while the other end of the spring is fixed at point O. If the body moves about O in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed 5 rad s −1 , then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be: (a) 1:2 (b) 1:1 (c) 2:3 (d) 2:5 — (JEE Main 2023)

A car is moving with a constant speed of 20 m s −1 on a circular horizontal track of radius 40 m. A bob is suspended from the roof of the car by a massless string. The angle made by the string with the vertical will be: (g = 10 m s −2 ) (a) π/6 (b) π/2 (c) π/4 (d) π/3 — (JEE Main 2023)

For particle P revolving round the centre O with radius of circular path r and regular velocity ω, as shown in the figure, the projection of OP on the x-axis at time t is (T = 6 s, P starts 30° above the x-axis): (a) x(t) = r cos(ωt − π/6) (b) x(t) = r cos(ωt + π/6) (c) x(t) = r sin(ωt + π/6) (d) x(t) = r cos(ωt) — (JEE Main 2023)

A car is moving on a horizontal curved road with radius 50 m. The approximate maximum speed of the car will be, if the friction between the tyres and the road is 0.34. [Take g = 10 m s −2 ] (a) 3.4 m s −1 (b) 22.4 m s −1 (c) 13 m s −1 (d) 17 m s −1 — (JEE Main 2023)

key: c A = 2/3, a constant — the horizontal-line graph, option (c)
stem: A ball is released from rest from point P of a smooth semi-spherical vessel as shown in the figure. The ratio of the centripetal force and the normal reaction on the ball at point Q is A, while the angular position of point Q is α with respect to point P. Which of the following graphs represents the correct relation between A and α when the ball goes from Q to R? — (JEE Main 2022)

A boy ties a stone of mass 100 g to the end of a 2 m long string and whirls it around in a horizontal plane. The string can withstand a maximum tension of 80 N. If the maximum speed with which the stone can revolve is (K/π) rev min −1 , the value of K is: (Assume the string is massless and un-stretchable) (a) 400 (b) 300 (c) 600 (d) 800 — (JEE Main 2022)

key: c minimum at the highest position
stem: A stone of mass m, tied to a string, is being whirled in a vertical circle with a uniform speed. The tension in the string is: (a) the same throughout the motion (b) minimum when the rope is in the horizontal position (c) minimum at the highest position of the circular path (d) minimum at the lowest position of the circular path — (JEE Main 2022)

A disc with a flat small bottom beaker placed on it at a distance R from its centre is revolving about an axis passing through the centre and perpendicular to its plane with an angular velocity ω. The coefficient of static friction between the bottom of the beaker and the surface of the disc is μ. The beaker will revolve with the disc if: (a) R ≤ μg/2ω² (b) R ≤ μg/ω² (c) R ≥ μg/2ω² (d) R ≥ μg/ω² — (JEE Main 2022)

Passage (Q21 & Q22): A smooth slot runs along a diameter of a disc of radius R rotating counter-clockwise with constant angular speed ω about its vertical axis through its centre. The X-axis is along the slot, the Y-axis perpendicular to it and the z-axis along the rotation axis (ω̄ = ωk̂). A small block of mass m is gently placed in the slot at r̄ = (R/2)î at t = 0 and is constrained to move only along the slot. — The distance r of the block at time t is: (a) (R/2)cos2ωt (b) (R/2)cosωt (c) (R/4)(e ωt +e −ωt ) (d) (R/4)(e 2ωt +e −2ωt ) — (JEE Advanced 2016)

key: b ½mω²R(e ωt − e −ωt )ĵ + mg k̂ ⚠
stem: The net reaction of the disc on the block is: (a) mω²R sinωt ĵ − mg k̂ (b) ½mω²R(e ωt − e −ωt )ĵ + mg k̂ (c) ½mω²R(e 2ωt − e −2ωt )ĵ + mg k̂ (d) −mω²R cosωt ĵ − mg k̂ — (JEE Advanced 2016)

A bob of mass m, suspended by a string of length ℓ 1 , is given a minimum velocity required to complete a full circle in the vertical plane. At the highest point, it collides elastically with another bob of mass m suspended by a string of length ℓ 2 , which is initially at rest. Both the strings are massless and inextensible. If the second bob, after collision, acquires the minimum speed required to complete a full circle in the vertical plane, the ratio ℓ 1 /ℓ 2 is: (a) 1 (b) 3 (c) 5 (d) 1/5 — (JEE Advanced 2014 Paper 2)

key: d radially inwards initially and radially outwards later
stem: A wire, which passes through the hole in a small bead, is bent in the form of a quarter of a circle. The wire is fixed vertically on the ground as shown in the figure. The bead is released from near the top of the wire and it slides along the wire without friction. As the bead moves from A to B, the force it applies on the wire is: (a) always radially outwards (b) always radially inwards (c) radially outwards initially and radially inwards later (d) radially inwards initially and radially outwards later — (JEE Advanced 2014 Paper 2)

Multiple Correct Answer Question. A student skates up a ramp that makes an angle 30° with the horizontal. He/she starts at the bottom of the ramp with speed v 0 and wants to turn around over a semicircular path xyz of radius R during which he/she reaches a maximum height h (at point y) from the ground as shown in the figure. Assume that the energy loss is negligible and the force required for this turn at the highest point is provided by his/her weight only. Then (g is the acceleration due to gravity): (a) v 0 ² − 2gh = ½gR (b) v 0 ² − 2gh = (√3/2)gR (c) the centripetal force required at points x and z is zero (d) the centripetal force required is maximum at points x and z — (JEE Advanced 2020)
